Elaborate the API for calling cpuset_zone_allowed()
explicitly choose between the two variants:
cpuset_zone_allowed_hardwall()
cpuset_zone_allowed_softwall()
Until now
column2: whether or not you got the hardwall flavor depended solely on

column1: whether or not you or'd in the __GFP_HARDWALL gfp flag to the gfp_mask
argument.
If you didn't specify __GFP_HARDWALL
version.
Unfortunately
column2: this meant that users would end up with the softwall version

column1: without thinking about it.  Since only the softwall version might sleep
this led to bugs with possible sleeping in interrupt context on more than
one occassion.
The hardwall version requires that the current tasks mems_allowed allows
the node of the specified zone (or that you're in interrupt or that
__GFP_THISNODE is set or that you're on a one cpuset system.)
The softwall version
column3: might allow a node if it

column1: was allowed in the nearest enclusing cpuset marked mem_exclusive (which
requires taking the cpuset lock 'callback_mutex' to evaluate.)
This patch removes the cpuset_zone_allowed() call
explicitly choose between the hardwall and the softwall case.
If the caller wants the gfp_mask to determine this choice
be sure they can sleep or that __GFP_HARDWALL is set
cpuset_zone_allowed_softwall() routine.
This adds another 100 or 200 bytes to the kernel text space
lines of nearly duplicate code at the top of both cpuset_zone_allowed_*
routines.  It should save a few instructions executed for the calls that
turned into calls of cpuset_zone_allowed_hardwall
set (before the call) then check (within the call) the __GFP_HARDWALL flag.
For the most critical call
instructions are executed as before -- the old cpuset_zone_allowed()
routine it used to call is the same code as the
cpuset_zone_allowed_softwall() routine that it calls now.
Not a perfect win
column3: to reduce this chance of hitting a

column1: sleeping with irq off complaint again.
